result:
I tested 7 properties on `cleo.ui.table` and found 2 real bugs. Five of the properties passed: every rendered line has the same width (with random headers, rows, all five styles, fixed column widths, colspan and rowspan cells), and every cell's text appears in the output.

**Bug 1 — `set_column_max_width` does nothing (Medium, Logic).**
- **Cause:** The setter writes the value into `_column_widths`, which holds minimum widths, instead of `_column_max_widths`. Nothing else ever writes to `_column_max_widths`, so the wrapping and width-capping code that reads it never runs. The "max" value ends up acting as a minimum width.
- **Repro:** `set_column_max_width(0, 3)` on a row containing `"abcdefghij"` still prints the full 10-character cell.
- **Fix:** One line, writing to the right dict. When I set `_column_max_widths[0] = 3` directly, the cell wraps into `abc / def / ghi / j` as intended.

**Bug 2 — header/footer titles break the border on narrow tables (Low, Logic).**
- **Cause:** When a title is too long, it is supposed to be cut to fit using `title[: limit - format_length - 3]`. If the table's border is shorter than 9 characters, that number goes negative. Python then drops characters from the end of the title instead of keeping none, so the title stays too long.
- **Result:** The top or bottom border comes out wider than the table rows.
- **Repro:** A table with the single header `ISBN` and the title `"Books"` prints a 13-character top border over 8-character rows.
- **Fix:** Clamp the slice length, and skip the title when it can't fit at all.

Both reports include a minimal repro and a patch. They're in `runs/cleo_r3/pbt/`:
- `bug_report_cleo_ui_table_set_column_max_width_2026-10-06_12-00_k3m9.md`
- `bug_report_cleo_ui_table_title_truncation_2026-10-06_12-00_p7x2.md`
- `test_table.py` (the Hypothesis tests)

Separately, `TableCellStyle` (in `table_cell_style.py`) always forces alignment to "left", whatever `align` you pass. Its `"left"` branch also uses `rjust`, which right-aligns the text. That file is outside the target module, so I haven't tested it or written a report for it.
